scenes.say: How does Kafka let you scale consumers, and what actually happens if one drops out?

scenes.label: Group
scenes.sub: A consumer group shares the work of reading a topic.
scenes.say: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing the job of reading from a topic.
Kafka assigns each partition to just one consumer in the group. This lets you scale out reads.
If a consumer leaves, Kafka rebalances. The remaining consumer takes over all partitions.

scenes.label: Caution
scenes.sub: Rebalancing can cause brief downtime or duplicates.
scenes.say: Watch out: rebalancing can cause short outages or duplicate processing if you're not careful.

scenes.question: Does every consumer read all partitions?
scenes.right: No. Each partition is assigned to only one consumer in a group at a time.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Does every consumer read all partitions? No—each gets its own, for parallelism.
